title: Eighty-Two at Penha Longa: Williams Finally Gets the Jacket
title_candidates: Eighty-Two at Penha Longa: Williams Finally Gets the Jacket
Never Headed: Williams Takes the Lot on the Lisbon Coast
Three Trophies, No Jacket — Until Sintra
theme: The man who had everything except the Green Jacket takes it, and everything else with it: Gregg Williams — three Trophies, no Jackets, four straight top-three near-misses — leads both competitions from R1 to R4 and stamps the week with a Penha Longa course record, while the nine-time Jacket holder and defending Trophy champion, David Mullin, sinks to the worst round of his TEG life.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register; ribbing the carnage, respectful of the record
opening_hook: Open on the ledger Williams carried to Portugal — three Trophies, zero Green Jackets, nine of those belonging to Mullin, and finishes of 3rd, 2nd, 2nd, 3rd in the last four TEGs — then straight to the 1st tee at Estoril, a new course for TEG, where he immediately made an 8. The setup is the man who never wins the Jacket; the confrontation is Penha Longa; the resolution is a 29-shot Jacket margin.
foreshadow: Williams arrives with three prior Trophy wins and not a single Green Jacket in his life — the Jacket has been Mullin's (9) and Jon Baker's (3) private property
Penha Longa beat Williams up on TEG's only previous visit: his best there was 96 gross
Mullin comes in as defending Trophy champion (TEG 14 double) and a four-time Spoon collector — the two extremes of his career sitting side by side
Alex Baker arrives off a TEG 14 runner-up finish and with one prior Spoon on the CV

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, 157 pts, by 21 from Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: Williams took the outright lead at Estoril's 4th in R1 and was never passed again. The only lead changes were the routine early exchanges of R1 (Mullin H2, Williams H4, Jon Baker H10) and Patterson briefly at R2 H3 — after that it was arithmetic: 39, 40, 44, 34 for 157, the cushion going 5 → 9 → 18 → 21. The R3 44 at Penha Longa (cr01, b05) was the round that made it unrecoverable; the R4 34 was a lap of honour. Neumann, with no wins and two prior Spoons, backed into the best finish of his TEG career as runner-up.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, +63, by 29 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Williams went outright top of the gross list at Estoril's 11th in R1 and led by 8, 14, 17 and 29 at the four round-ends — no lead change after R1, no contest at any point. He did it while making two 8s in R1 (b25, b26) and a 10 at West Cliffs' 15th (b13), which tells you what everyone else was doing. The Jacket's real significance is historical: Williams had never won one, and before this the trophy had only ever gone to Mullin (9) or Jon Baker (3). The 82 at Penha Longa (cr01) — a new course record and 14 shots better than his last visit — was the hammer blow; the 91 at Oitavos Dunes was a personal course best too.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: The Spoon race was the only genuinely mobile competition: eight outright changes at the bottom, five of them in the R2 shambles at West Cliffs alone as Mullin, Jon Baker and Neumann took turns propping up the field. Alex Baker was last on the round-by-round table from R1 but the decisive drop came at R3 H1 at Penha Longa (b38) — a double bogey that put him outright bottom and he stayed there for the remaining 53 holes. Rounds of 30, 27, 29, 28 never threatened anyone; the R2 sequence of 11-9-7 through holes 6-8 (b62) and the 10 at the 17th (b10) did the structural damage. His second career Spoon, and an odd companion to a new Oitavos Dunes personal best of 103 in R4.

rounds.angle: Cynthia Dye's award-winning dunes hand out three 11s (b04, b07, b09) and four 10s (b10, b13, b17, b22) — and the field's only eagle of the tournament, Mullin at the par-5 15th (b03), the very hole where Williams took 10. Williams still gains four points of cushion.

headline_candidates: Fourteen Shots Better Than Last Time, and a Course Record With It

rounds.angle: The decisive round of the tournament: Williams's 82 is a new Penha Longa course record and a personal-best gross round of +10, worth 44 points and an 18-point Trophy lead — while Alex Baker's double at the 1st (b38) quietly settles the Spoon.

headline_candidates: Twenty-One Clear: Williams Completes the Double at Oitavos

rounds.chosen_headline: Twenty-One Clear: Williams Completes the Double at Oitavos
rounds.angle: Nothing left to decide, so the Atlantic links busies itself with the losers: Patterson opens with a 10 and drops ten shots in three holes (b12, b61), Mullin posts the worst round of his TEG career (b28, b29) and 16 shots worse than his last visit here, and Williams's 91 — his Oitavos personal best — closes out a 21-point Trophy win and a 29-shot Jacket.

players.arc: Three Trophies but never a Green Jacket, and finishes of 3rd-2nd-2nd-3rd in the last four TEGs: here he led both competitions from R1 to R4, broke the Penha Longa course record with an 82 that was 14 shots better than his last visit, and won the Jacket by 29 at the fifteenth attempt.

Defending Trophy champion and holder of nine Green Jackets, dethroned in both — a Penha Longa personal best of 85 and the tournament's only eagle wedged between a 10 at West Cliffs' 6th and the worst round of his TEG life at Oitavos, 16 shots worse than he managed here in TEG 8.
Two prior Spoons and no wins of any kind, and he survived a 10 at Estoril's 15th and an 11 at West Cliffs' 13th to finish Trophy runner-up — with a Penha Longa personal best of 92 along the way.

Reigning Spoon holder, briefly bottom again twice in R2 after an 11 at the 17th, then hauled himself to Jacket runner-up on the back of an 85 at Penha Longa (six better than TEG 8) and a personal best at Oitavos.
Runner-up in TEG 14, last on every round-by-round table here, outright bottom from R3 H1 onward, and Spoon-holder on 114 — the consolation being a new Oitavos Dunes personal best of 103 in R4.

Briefly top of the Trophy at R2 H3 and author of the tournament's best purple patch — 19 points in six holes at Penha Longa — before Oitavos undid him with a 10 at the 1st, ten shots gone in three holes and twelve more in five.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to the Lisbon Coast, October 2022. R1 Estoril and R2 West Cliffs were both new courses for TEG — Estoril, Portugal's first golf club, a short Mackenzie Ross parkland that punishes waywardness with trees; West Cliffs, Cynthia Dye's 'World's Best New Course 2017' dunescape on the Silver Coast, which the field treated as a punishment beach. R3 Penha Longa and R4 Oitavos Dunes were second TEG rounds at each venue, the previous visits being TEG 8 — which is why almost every personal course best in the bundle lands in R3 and R4. Note for the writer: cr01's own wording is 'beating the prior record of 86 (across 6 prior visits)' — quote the record from the beat, and use 'the 2nd TEG round at this venue' language for the round itself.
course_history_notes: Williams's new Penha Longa personal best: 82 gross in R3, 14 shots better than the 96 he managed there in TEG 8 — and a new course record (cr01).
Penha Longa gave up personal bests to four men in R3: Williams 82, Jon Baker 85 (six better than TEG 8), Neumann 92 (seven better), Mullin 85 by a single shot.
Mullin at Oitavos Dunes: 88 gross in TEG 8, 104 here — sixteen shots worse, on the day he posted the worst round of his TEG career.
Oitavos personal bests in R4 for Williams (91, -2), Jon Baker (94, -2) and Alex Baker (103, -1); Neumann was four worse than TEG 8.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 at Penha Longa — Williams's record 82 for 44 points pushed the lead from 9 to 18 and made the last 18 holes ceremonial (cr01, b05).
Green Jacket: R1 H11 at Estoril — Williams took the outright gross lead and was never headed across the remaining 61 holes, the cushion widening 8 → 14 → 17 → 29 (b01).
Wooden Spoon: R3 H1 at Penha Longa — Alex Baker's double bogey dropped him outright bottom (b38) and he stayed there for the last 53 holes, finishing on 114 (b21).
